Buffered Bike Lanes
Class II Buffered Bike Lanes are implemented by
painting or otherwise creating a buffer zone between
a bicycle lane and the adjacent travel lane.
Buffered Bike Lane—Ivy Hill Wy.
New Bike Lane—Old Crow Canyon Rd./Crow Canyon Rd.

Green Conflict Markings
Green Conflict Markings, commonly known as “Conflict
Zones” are colored markings that help alert vehicles of
areas where the bicycle path and vehicle path intersect.
Conflict Zones are used at intersections and major drive-
ways, where a right turning vehicle would cross the
through the bicycle movement.
Green Conflict Zone—Crow Canyon Rd./Canyon Crest Dr.
Shared Lane Marking/Sharrows
Shared Lane Marking or “Sharrow” is a pavement marking
used to indicate a shared lane environment for bicycles
and automobiles. Among other benefits, Sharrows rein-
force the legitimacy of bicycle traffic on the street, recom-
mend proper bicyclist positioning to avoid hazards such
as opening of doors from parked vehicles, provides a
wayfinding guidance along bike routes, and reduces the
incidence of wrong-way bicycling. The Sharrow has a
variety of uses to support a complete bikeway network in
San Ramon.
Sharrows—Montevideo Dr./Alcosta Blvd.

Bike Boxes
A Bike Box is a designated area between the limit line and
the queue of stopped vehicles at a signalized intersection,
which allows bicyclists in the bike lane to safely position
themselves before making a left turn.
Bike Box and Green Conflict Zone at Bishop Dr./Sunset Dr.
San Ramon Bike Infrastructure Stats
Since adoption of the Bicycle Master Plan, San Ramon
has installed approximately 6,200 feet (1.2 mi.) of Green
Conflict Markings and 104,500 feet (19.8 mi.) of buffered
bike lanes, totaling 21 miles of improvement in the net-
work, 2 new Class II bike lanes, and a bike box.
New Buffered Bike Lane—Executive Pkwy.
